commits.message:
test(docs): follow the receivers a static factory produces (rich-docs-site-13t.6.5) (#87)

A variable was recorded only when its initializer was `new X()`, so a name
bound from a static factory entered no declaration list, resolved to no root,
and every member called on it was dropped without a report. `docs/tables.md`'s
whole grid section and `docs/style.md`'s `Style.parse` section were outside the
gate, and a ghost method on either would have passed.

A binding now carries the receiver chain its initializer describes rather than
a class name, which is the same thing `describeReceiver` already computed for
a use — the guard was discarding an answer the parser had in hand. Resolution
follows those chains back recursively, and a bare imported name the page
declared nothing for resolves to the class object itself. A class has two
member sets, instance and statics, and only step zero of a chain may read the
static one; everything after a factory is an instance again.

Widening the gate found two things the old one could not see. `RichText.fromAnsi`
does not exist and never has, so `docs/text.md`'s "Building from ANSI codes"
section is deleted rather than implemented. `docs/console.md` binds `output` to
an array in one section and to `console.endCapture()` in another, which surfaced
a hole the widening opened: a declaration that binds nothing followable still
takes the name, or the fallback-forward rule hands it an unrelated declaration
elsewhere on the page.

Both static-factory forms are pinned by fixtures rather than by the corpus.
Reverting the guard alone leaves all 37 corpus tests green and turns four
fixtures red, which is the whole argument for having them.

Also: `docs/live.md` claimed a file-based console emits only when "the context"
exits. There is no context on that page any more, and the claim was false in
both halves — `Live` never checks whether its console is a terminal and writes
every frame it draws. And `docs/.vitepress/sidebar.ts` claimed the reachability
check has no exclusion predicate; `test/docs/pages.ts` has one on the disk
side, so the claim is now scoped to the sidebar side it is true of.
